definition: The Culture is a fictional interstellar post-scarcity society created by the Scottish writer Iain M.
details: Banks and features in a number of his space opera novels and works of short fiction, collectively called the Culture series. The Culture is composed primarily of humanoid aliens, artificial intelligences (A.I.), and a number of other sentient life forms. The A.I. intelligence covers a spectrum; simple programs performing a specific function (e.g. controlling spacesuits), human-equivalent drones and hyper-intelligent Minds who organise and oversee the society. Beyond scarcity, the Culture has no need for money; instead, Minds organise society to maximise the well-being of its citizenry. The protagonists, almost always humanoids, are generally those who have chosen to work for the Culture's diplomatic or espionage organs and interact with other civilisations whose citizens act under different ideologies, morals, and technologies. The Culture generally has more advanced technology relative to most other civilisations it shares the galaxy with. Most of the Culture's citizens do not live on planets but in artificial habitats such as orbitals and ships, the largest of which are home to billions of individuals. explainer.lead: A fictional interstellar post-scarcity society created by Iain M. Banks, spanning his Culture novels and short fiction. It matters in AI discourse for its spectrum of artificial intelligences, from simple suit-controlling programs to the hyper-intelligent Minds that organise the society.

tiers.eli5: Think of a whole civilisation where the boring jobs are done by helpful robots and the big decisions are made by very, very smart computers, so people are free to do whatever they like.
tiers.practitioner: Often invoked when discussing benign superintelligence or post-scarcity governance; the pitfall is treating a literary setting as an engineering or policy proposal.
tiers.paperLevel: No formal definition exists; the Culture is characterised by post-scarcity and by AIs covering a spectrum from single-function programs through human-equivalent drones to Minds that organise and oversee the society. Its limits are those of fiction: no mechanisms, metrics, or failure analysis.

explainer.example: A spacesuit-controlling program and a Mind that runs a whole orbital are both AIs within the same fictional society, illustrating the breadth of the spectrum.
